source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #276 (branch fix/270-wait-timer-release at head 276a0e41ff732ad12d66df383ea48dc88b35c692 — branch commit 278de94 (release atomic.wait timer threads when the wait resolves) plus merge commit 276a0e4 bringing in current main 92b66b3, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45169595430 and 45169601657 against the branch and pull-request run 45169582070, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #276 (#270, atomic.wait timer threads are released when the wait resolves: SharedWaiter gains a release (Mutex, Condvar) pair signalled by the successful CAS claim in try_mark_notified / try_mark_interrupted; the per-wait timer thread sleeps in the condvar's wait_timeout and exits as soon as the wait is resolved instead of sleeping to the original deadline, and registrations already resolved before wait_result is polled spawn no thread at all). The branch merged current main (92b66b3, containing PRs #269, #273, #278 and #275) before measurement; the merge was conflict-free (main's only change to common/memory.rs was the push_to_stack visibility narrowing from PR #269, disjoint from the wait-timer code). The first CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate on this PR's own change. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (92b66b3) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45169608064, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. The growth is confined to wasi-threads, the configuration with the threads feature that compiles the shared-wait timer code in crates/telomere/src/common/memory.rs: release stripped file +1,608 B / stripped .text +1,280 B; release-size +1,088 B / +800 B. The other 30 gated series are byte-identical; 2 of the 32 gated series change. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.41% (1,169,031 B to 1,232,247 B), unchanged, because that series does not move here. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (16 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
